## Problem

The LSP server calls `package_require_actions` unconditionally for every code-action request. The provider extracts whichever identifier-like word is under the cursor, fuzzy-matches its prefix against the registry package catalogue, and offers `Add 'package require …'` without requiring W120/W123, an unknown command, or executable command-head context.

For example, a cursor on `http::geturl` in any of these can offer `package require http`:

```tcl
# Documentation: http::geturl
set example "http::geturl"
dict set docs command http::geturl
proc http::geturl {} {}
http::geturl
```

Only the final call might need a package, and even it may be a local definition, rename, alias, imported command, or `unknown`-resolved command. The first three are data. This is a false-positive quick fix rather than a harmless completion: applying it mutates package loading and can run package initialisation code.

## Root cause

`tcl-lsp-server::code_action` always extends actions with `package_require_actions`. The provider uses `word_at_position` and registry package names, but receives neither the request diagnostics nor a resolved command invocation.

W120 already carries a precise registry-derived insertion fix. The fuzzy provider duplicates that mechanism at a weaker precision level.

## Fix direction

Prefer one generic path:

1. Lift the CodeFix attached to an overlapping W120/W123 diagnostic.
2. If fuzzy recovery remains useful, gate it on a proven command-head invocation which resolution classifies as unresolved and on the diagnostic supplied in `CodeActionContext`.
3. Resolve leading `::`, namespaces, imports, static `rename`/`interp alias`, safe/sub-interpreter visibility, and package state through shared analyser/registry facts.
4. Never infer executable context by string scanning.

## Tests and acceptance

- TP: unresolved registered package command, including qualified and namespace-import shapes.
- FP: comments, quoted/braced data, argument words, local proc definitions, renamed/aliased commands, already-loaded packages, and disabled W120/W123.
- TN: dynamic heads, `unknown`, safe interpreters, unsupported dialect/version, and unregistered local packages.
- FN: static imports, source/package workspace evidence, and leading-`::` package commands.
- Add core tests which assert the absence of actions, native code-action e2e coverage using the real diagnostic context, and VS Code lightbulb/apply tests.
- Document that package suggestions are evidence-backed and can have package-initialisation side effects.

Do not add clippy allows. Package/command knowledge must remain registry data; the LSP should consume resolved facts generically.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Default minifier drops valid `switch` arms whose pattern begins with `#`
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

A braced `switch` case list is a Tcl **list**, not a script. In a list, `#` has no comment meaning.

Reproducer:

```tcl
switch # {
    # {puts matched}
    default {puts default}
}
```

C Tcl 9.0.3 prints:

```text
matched
```

Current default minification produces:

```tcl
switch # {default {puts default}}
```

which prints `default`.

`minify_switch_case_list` tokenises the list with the Tcl script lexer and skips `TokenType::Comment`. The lexer therefore discards the real `#` pattern and its body through end-of-line. This violates the default tier's documented semantic-equivalence guarantee; aggressive minification inherits it.

The formatter has the related precision smell of treating list `#` words as comment elements, even where it happens to preserve the flattened elements.

## Fix direction

Use the central Tcl list parser for every registry-declared list-valued grammar. Decode pattern/body pairs as list elements, recursively minify only body elements, and re-encode with the shared list-element renderer. Preserve the original list if it is malformed, dynamically constructed, odd-length beyond Tcl's allowed fall-through rules, or exceeds recursion limits.

Do not special-case the spelling `switch` in the minifier. Add a registry descriptor for alternating pattern/body list grammar and let generic consumers use it; this should also cover dialect commands with equivalent list grammars.

## Tests and acceptance

- Execute original/minified output under C Tcl 9 and compare output, result, error code, and side effects.
- TP: `#` pattern, patterns containing spaces/backslashes/semicolons, `-` fall-through, `default`, options, `-matchvar`/`-indexvar`, and nested bodies.
- FP/TN/FN: quoted/braced `#`, malformed and odd lists, dynamic case lists, qualified/static aliases, renamed `switch`, and same-named user commands.
- Add default/compact/aggressive minifier tests, native execute-command e2e, VS Code minify tests, and corpus differential execution.
- Document list-versus-script parsing in plain English.

Do not add clippy allows.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: `workspace/symbol` clones the entire open-document map and serially re-analyses every open document per keystroke, while ignoring the `WorkspaceIndex` that already has the answer
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
`workspace/symbol` (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs:11081–11091`) does `self.documents.lock().await.clone()` — the whole map, every text + `LineIndex` — then per document clones the text again, awaits `analysis_for` and a `spawn_blocking` round-trip **serially**. VS Code sends `workspace/symbol` on every keystroke in the Ctrl+T box; 30 open tabs = 30 full-map clones' worth of memory traffic + 30 sequential blocking-pool round-trips per keystroke, with no result cap.

It also only searches *open* documents — `workspace_index` (which already holds every proc/class/method for the whole workspace with `name`, `qualified_name`, `uri`, `name_span`; `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/workspace_index.rs:684–697`) is never consulted — so the feature is simultaneously slow and incomplete: symbols in unopened files are invisible.

Fix: answer from `workspace_index`, filter before materialising, cap results (~1000). No document text or analysis needed.

Found by an opus static audit.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: The `!script_is_complete` recovery branch — the normal mid-typing state — bypasses all memoisation: O(workspace symbols) allocations plus a full uncached, non-cancellable analysis per debounced run
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
While a delimiter is open — i.e. for the whole time the user is typing a new `proc foo {` / `if {…} {` block — `compute_base_analysis` takes the `!tcl_lexer::script_is_complete(text)` branch (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs:1051–1081`) on every debounced run. That branch, via `widen_recovery_extra_commands` (`lib.rs:1162–1202`): iterates every workspace-indexed proc and class calling `insert_qualified_and_tail` (3 `String` allocations each — ~60k allocations per edit on tcllib's ~20k procs) into a fresh `HashSet`; allocates a `String` per `auto_command_names()` entry; runs a full `extract_signatures` scan of the document; possibly reads and scans package implementation files from disk; and then runs a completely uncached, non-salsa, **non-cancellable** `Analyser::analyse` over the whole file (`lib.rs:1063–1067`, with a redundant deep `.clone()` on top).

So the single most common editing state is exactly the one that opts out of `file_analysis_incremental`, per-item memoisation, and salsa cancellation.

Fix: cache the widened name-set keyed on the workspace-index `generation` (it changes when the index does, not per keystroke); memoise the recovery analysis through salsa keyed on `(text, dialect, widened_set_generation)` so a keystroke burst inside one unterminated block reuses per-item results; at minimum make the recovery path cancellable so a superseding edit unwinds it.

Found by an opus static audit.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: `codeLens` is O(procs × workspace index) per request with nothing cached, and `codeLens/resolve` recomputes the whole document's lenses per lens — default-on and re-requested after every edit
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
`code_lenses` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/code_lens.rs:137–183`) calls `index.invocations_of(qualified_name, current_uri)` once per proc (`:148`) and once per class (`:181`). Each call lands in `invocations_settling_to` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/workspace_index.rs:2241–2260`), which per invocation rebuilds `defined_command_names` (a `HashSet` over ALL procs+classes), optionally `command_link_map`, and `WildcardImportIndex::build` (5 HashMaps over the whole index), then scans ALL invocations. None of it is cached. On `practcl.tcl` (114 procs) inside tcllib that is 114 × (O(20k symbols) + O(whole index) + O(all invocations)) ≈ 10⁷–10⁸ operations per `textDocument/codeLens` request — which VS Code re-issues after every edit, and the feature is default-on (absent from `FeatureToggles::DEFAULT_OFF`, `rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs:2657–2662`).

`code_lens_resolve` (`lib.rs:11417–11426`) then re-runs the **entire** `code_lenses` walk per resolved lens, plus `reference_locations_at` (`lib.rs:11442`) — a full find-all-references including cross-document scans. A screenful of 20 lenses = 20 whole-document lens computations + 20 full reference resolutions. (The `workspace_class_analyses` memo comment at `lib.rs:2482–2483` records this shape measured at 0.31 s per lens over 40 consumer documents.)

Fix: build `defined_command_names` / `command_link_map` / `WildcardImportIndex` once per index generation and cache on the index (the `generation`/`invalidate` + `CommandNameCache`/`LiveLinkCache` machinery exists for exactly this); add an `invocations_by_settled_target: HashMap<String, Vec<usize>>` derived cache so `invocations_of` is a hash lookup; make `code_lens_resolve` compute only the single named lens (it already has the qualified name).

Found by an opus static audit.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: `WorkspaceIndex::remove_document` is a 14-way linear scan of the whole workspace index, run 2–3× per keystroke under the `documents` lock — typing latency scales with workspace size, not file size
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
`WorkspaceIndex::remove_document` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/workspace_index.rs:1267–1283`) does 14 `Vec::retain` passes with a `String` compare per element. `invocations` and `variable_refs` hold one record per call site / variable reference across the whole workspace — order 10⁵–10⁶ records on tcllib (325k LoC) — and `retain` memmoves them too. Call sites on the hot path: `did_change` (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs:9516–9519`, while holding the `documents` mutex and the index write lock) and `publish_diagnostics_result` (`lib.rs:2203–2206`, remove + add per publish, also under `documents`). `invalidate()` (`workspace_index.rs:803–807`) additionally drops the `command_names` and `live_links` caches on each call, forcing `command_names()` (3 `insert_qualified_and_tail` allocations per proc/class over ~20k procs) to rebuild on the next deep-diagnostics pass.

Because it runs under `documents`, every request handler stalls behind it as well.

Related retention nit (same structure): `remove_document`'s `retain` never reduces `Vec` capacity, so the index holds its high-water-mark allocation for the process lifetime.

Fix: key the index by URI — `HashMap<Uri, DocumentEntry>` holding that document's records, with per-kind global views derived lazily (or ranges into flat vecs with tombstones + periodic compaction). `remove_document` then becomes O(that document's records). Also drop the removal from `did_change` entirely — `publish_diagnostics_result` already does remove+add; the edit path only needs the entry marked stale. Cache-generation machinery for derived sets already exists (`generation`/`invalidate`, `CommandNameCache`/`LiveLinkCache` as the template).

Found by an opus static audit.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Unify Tcl dialect gating for commands, operators, and functions into one registry-driven mechanism
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

Command/subcommand availability per Tcl dialect (8.4/8.5/8.6/9.0/9.1, iRules, BIG-IP Tcl, etc.) is currently decided by at least six independent, disconnected mechanisms instead of one:

1. `CommandSpec.dialects: Option<DialectSet>` on ordinary commands (`rust/tcl-registry/src/spec.rs`), resolved through `CommandRegistry::spec_visible`/`best_visible`/`get_for_dialect` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs`).
2. `IRULES_DISABLED_COMMANDS`, a subtractive ban list in `rust/tcl-dialect/src/profile.rs` used only for iRules-specific removals that aren't expressible as a version-gate (contract-tested by `irules_disable_list_is_load_bearing` in `rust/tcl-registry/tests/dialect_profile.rs`, which exists specifically to keep the list from silently absorbing version gating that belongs on the `dialects` axis instead).
3. `DialectProfile::operators_as_commands: bool` + `Traits::OPERATOR_COMMAND`, gating whether `tcl::mathop::*` names are callable as ordinary commands.
4. `tcl_syntax::expr::mathfunc::added_in`/`MathFuncSince`, gating `expr` math functions by version (feeds diagnostic W002 via `emit_expr_function_dialect_diagnostics`/`math_func_ceiling_for_dialect`).
5. `GATED_EXPR_OPS` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs`, a hand-maintained table gating `expr` grammar keywords (`in`/`ni`/`**` at 8.5+, `lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge` at 9.0+) — diagnostic W003.
6. `DialectProfile::is_irules(): bool`, a single boolean with no version axis at all, gating the iRules-only word operators (`contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `matches_glob`, `matches_regex`) in the expr lexer/parser/evaluator.

These six mechanisms don't share data, don't share a diagnostic code space consistently, and don't share a single "what does dialect X actually have" query surface. That's let real bugs land silently — each one below is a direct consequence of one of these mechanisms having no single source of truth:

- **mathop registry data bugs** — bad entries went into (3)'s table without being cross-checked against the runtimes it's supposed to describe.
- **iRules operator dialect gating gap** — mechanism (6) has no check at the evaluation site at all; it accepts and evaluates the iRules word operators regardless of dialect.
- **duplicate hardcoded operator lists** — LSP-facing features (semantic tokens, completion) each re-derive "what's an operator" from scratch, because there's no single query that already answers it.
- **missing drift gate** — no automated check that (3)/(4)/(5) actually match what the runtimes implement, unlike the equivalent gate that already exists for ordinary commands.

Filed as separate, independently-actionable sub-issues below (each fixable without waiting on this one).

## Proposed direction

The registry already has a generic-dispatch pattern that solves exactly this class of problem for `oo::define` body grammars: `DefinitionBodyGrammar`/`MemberSpec`/`MemberKind` in `rust/tcl-registry/src/definer.rs`, walked generically by `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/oo_body.rs` — registry data drives behavior, with no hardcoded keyword lists at the call sites. The typed hook-ID enums (`LoweringHookId`, `CodegenHookId`, `InlineCodegenHookId`, `AnalyserHookId`, `WasmCodegenHookId` in `rust/tcl-registry/src/hooks.rs`) are a similar closed-registry pattern solving a different axis (behavior dispatch rather than availability).

The suggested direction is a single closed table, keyed by operator/function/word-operator name, carrying per entry: which dialects/versions it's available in, whether it's a real command name (`tcl::mathop::*`) vs. grammar-only, and which runtimes actually implement it. `ProfileQueries` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/profile_queries.rs`) would gain the query methods needed so that W002/W003, the LSP hardcoded-list call sites, and the iRules operator evaluator all resolve dialect-gating through the same table instead of five or six independently-maintained ones.

This is intentionally a design/tracking issue, not a finished spec — the sub-issues below are independently actionable today and don't need to wait for the full unification to land.

## Related

See also #968 — a concrete bug that fell out of this same fragmentation (math-function dialect gating living in its own island, mechanism 4 above, rather than a shared table).

uncatalogued_candidates.title: No drift gate compares registry operator/function entries against what the runtimes actually implement
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
Part of #983.

## Summary

`xtask` already has a drift gate for ordinary commands — `cargo xtask command-backing` (see `xtask/src/command_backing.rs`) — which checks that every `CommandSpec` in the registry is actually backed by an implementation in the runtime(s) it claims to support, including a WASM-parity check (the `is_expr_operator`/`BARE` array around line 225-236 already treats expr operators as a special case there).

No equivalent gate exists for `tcl::mathop::*` or `tcl::mathfunc::*` entries specifically — nothing automatically compares the registry's operator/function name set against what `tcl-cmd-core`, `tcl-vm`, and the WASM (`runtime/rust`) runtime actually implement for those two namespaces. That's the direct reason the mathop bugs in the companion issue (missing `lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge`, bogus `&&`/`||`/`@`) were able to land and stay unnoticed — there was no automated check that would have failed.

## Suggested fix

Extend `xtask/src/command_backing.rs` (or add a sibling gate) to specifically enumerate `tcl::mathop::*` and `tcl::mathfunc::*` registry entries and cross-check each one against `tcl-cmd-core`/`tcl-vm`/`runtime/rust`, the same way the existing gate does for ordinary commands, using the existing `is_expr_operator`/`BARE` pattern as the template. This would have caught both data bugs in the companion mathop issue at CI time instead of requiring source-level cross-referencing to discover after the fact.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: fact_live_for_call's body-call escape hatch only checks one level of enclosing-definition indirection
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Background

Same root-cause class as #973/#1006/#1007/#1009/#1010/#1013: a "known command" check with a documented, narrower-than-real-Tcl scope limit. Found while fixing two Codex review comments on PR #1014 (the `finalise_invocation_resolutions` / `fact_live_for_call` call-site-lifetime bugs).

That fix added an escape hatch for a call *inside* a proc/class body whose enclosing definition has a provable *top-level* invocation before a later unconditional deletion (`Analyser::top_level_call_offsets`, consulted by `KnownPredicateCtx::live_for_call` in `scope.rs` and `Analyser::fact_live_for_call` in `unresolved.rs`). It only checks the *immediate* enclosing definition's own top-level call offset — it does not recurse through a chain of nested enclosing definitions.

## Confirmed (via tclsh 8.6.14 and the analyser's own test harness)

```tcl
proc helper {} { return hi }
proc inner {} { helper }
proc outer {} { inner }
outer
rename helper {}
```

tclsh 8.6.14: prints nothing but exits 0 — `outer`'s own top-level invocation (which calls `inner`, which calls `helper`) runs before the `rename helper {}`, so the whole chain resolves fine.

The analyser (after the #1014 review-comment fix): still emits `W123` on the `helper` call inside `inner`'s body, because `inner` is never itself invoked at the top level — only `outer` is, and `outer`'s own top-level call site isn't checked when deciding whether the `helper` reference (nested two bodies deep) is live.

## Why this wasn't folded into the #1014 fix

A fully correct escape hatch needs proper call-graph reachability: for a call inside definition D's body, find whether *any* chain of enclosing definitions — bottomed out at a genuine top-level call — proves D reachable before the deletion. That requires:

- A memoized/fixed-point computation over the (proc/class) call graph, not a single `HashMap` lookup.
- Cycle handling: mutual recursion (`proc a {} { b }`, `proc b {} { a }`, neither ever called at top level) must terminate as "unreachable," not loop forever.
- Deciding how deep to search when a definition is called from multiple sites, some conditional/never-triggered and some real.

This is meaningfully bigger and riskier than the one-level fix that resolved the two confirmed Codex findings, so it's tracked separately rather than rushed into that PR while CI was being driven to green.

## What the fix likely looks like

Generalize `top_level_call_offsets: HashMap<qualified_name, u32>` into a recursive `earliest_reachable_offset(qualified_name) -> Option<u32>` query:

- Base case: a genuine top-level (non-body) call site → that offset.
- Recursive case: for every call site to `qualified_name` that's itself inside some enclosing definition `E`'s body, candidate = `earliest_reachable_offset(E)`.
- Answer = min over all candidates, `None` if empty.
- Memoize per `qualified_name` with a visited-set to short-circuit cycles as `None` (unreachable via this path) rather than recursing forever.

Shared by both consumers (`scope.rs`'s `KnownPredicateCtx::live_for_call` and `unresolved.rs`'s `fact_live_for_call`) the same way the one-level version is today.

## Verification bar

- The repro above must not draw W123 after the fix.
- Regression guards: the existing one-level tests (`w123_fp_issue_1009_codex_review_body_call_before_later_deletion_resolves`, `w123_tp_issue_1009_codex_review_escape_hatch_requires_specific_enclosing_call`, and the `scope.rs` unit tests `local_call_before_later_deletion_resolves_local_not_global_codex_1009` / `local_call_after_deletion_still_falls_back_to_global_issue_973` / `escape_hatch_requires_the_specific_enclosing_definitions_own_top_level_call`) must all still pass.
- A mutual-recursion cycle (neither proc ever called at top level) must still draw W123 (or at least must not hang/loop).
- Confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available, 9.0).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## References

- Discovered while fixing PR #1014's Codex review comments (same root-cause class, deeper recursion case).
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs` (`KnownPredicateCtx`, `compute_top_level_call_offsets`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/unresolved.rs` (`fact_live_for_call`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/types.rs` (`enclosing_definition_qualified_name`).

uncatalogued_candidates.title: array get skips element read traces in both Tcl runtimes
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Reproduction

```tcl
set events {}
set a(x) X
proc tr {n1 n2 op} {
    lappend ::events [list $n1 $n2 $op]
    set ::a($n2) traced
}
trace add variable a(x) read tr
list [array get a] $events
```

Tcl 9.0.4 returns `{x traced} {{a x read}}`; both native `tclvm --tcl-version 9.0` and `runtime/rust` return `{x X} {}`. Whole-array read traces are missed as well.

## Root cause

The shared `tcl_cmd_core::array::get` path snapshots keys and reads each value with the storage-only `VarStore::get_elem`. Tcl uses a trace-aware element read for each captured key.

## Required fix

Add one shared trace-aware array-element read/iteration contract used by both runtimes. Preserve Tcl 9.0.4 semantics: snapshot keys from the located array, read through the live spelling, fire containing-array then element read traces, skip a missing element while the captured cell remains an array, and error if that captured array ceases to be an array. uncatalogued_candidates.title: A metaclass created under a computed name is never indexed — tcllib's `oo::dialect` / clay / practcl resolve nothing
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Summary

A metaclass whose *name* is a computed word (`Meta create ${ns}::class {…}`) never enters the workspace class-factory index, so every class it later manufactures is invisible. This is the shape tcllib's `oo::dialect` uses, which means clay, practcl, and everything built on them resolve nothing.

Found while verifying #1296 against the #1181 corpus. Distinct from #1296 (chain depth) and from #1304 (unopened files): here the name was never proved at all, so no number of publish rounds can recover it.

## The corpus instance

`tcllib/modules/oodialect/oodialect.tcl` and its copies in `clay.tcl` / `practcl.tcl`:

```tcl
# oodialect.tcl:251 — this level IS indexed and works cross-file
::oo::class create ::oo::dialect::MotherOfAllMetaClasses {
    superclass ::oo::class
    …
}

# oodialect.tcl:114, inside proc ::oo::dialect::create — this level does not
::oo::class create ${NSPACE}::class {
    superclass … ::oo::dialect::MotherOfAllMetaClasses
}
```

`::clay::class`, `::practcl::class`, and every per-language dialect metaclass are created this way, so none of them is ever a known factory and `clay::class create WidgetClass {…}` records nothing.

The level-1 metaclass genuinely works — a direct `::clay::dialect::MotherOfAllMetaClasses create ::MomMade {…}` cross-file resolves. It is only the computed-name link that breaks.

## Isolation

Same three-file chain, only the metaclass's name differs:

| Metaclass created as | Result |
|---|---|
| `::T::Mother create ::T::D::class { … }` (literal) | **1 location** ✓ |
| `::T::Mother create ${ns}::class { … }` (computed, inside a proc) | **0 locations** ✗ |

## Reproduction

```tcl
# t1.tcl
namespace eval ::T {}
oo::class create ::T::Mother { superclass oo::class }
proc ::T::mkdialect {ns} {
    ::T::Mother create ${ns}::class { superclass ::T::Mother }
}
::T::mkdialect ::T::D

# t2.tcl
::T::D::class create ::T::W { method go {} { return went } }

# t3.tcl
set w [::T::W new]
puts [$w go]
```

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/lsp-client/lsp_client.py \
  --server-dir /path/to/fixture --server-bin target/debug/tcl-lsp-server \
  --also-open t1.tcl --also-open t2.tcl definition t3.tcl 1 10
```

→ `=== Definition (0 locations) ===`. Replace the proc with a literal
`::T::Mother create ::T::D::class { superclass ::T::Mother }` → **1 location**.

Verified on `claude/tickets-1293-1296-registry-wpvi21` at 0e49243.

## Is the current behaviour wrong?

Abstaining is the *right* default — `is_dynamic_word` rejects the name and the analyser refuses to guess, which is the documented contract (see `kcs-issue-classes-made-by-a-class-factory-are-invisible.md`, decision rule 2). This ticket is not asking for a guess.

But the name here is statically determined in practice, which is exactly the class of case that KCS note exists to catch: `::T::mkdialect ::T::D` passes a literal, so `${ns}::class` is `::T::D::class` and nothing about it is unknowable until run time. The note's own framing — "a name is *written* dynamically but is in fact statically determined" — describes this precisely; the existing machinery just does not follow a literal argument through a proc parameter into a creation call.

## Suggested direction

This needs the creation call's name word to be resolved through the proc's parameter binding when every call site passes a literal — related to the existing const/literal propagation the analyser already does for `foreach` over a literal list (`Traits::INSTALLS_NAMED_DEFINITION`). Where a parameter is not uniformly literal across call sites, abstaining stays correct.

Per AGENTS.md this must stay registry/analyser data — no special-casing `oo::dialect` or `clay` by name.

## Related

- #1296 — chain depth (fixed; not this).
- #1304 — cross-file metaclass needs the defining file open (not this).
- #1303 — handle bound via a metaclass `unknown` dispatch (not this).

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Interprocedural taint summaries rerun dataflow 15× per parameter
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

`tcl-compiler/src/taint_interproc.rs::infer_proc_summary` computes a procedure’s return transfer function by re-running the full intraprocedural taint propagation once for the clean base and then once for every `(parameter, basis)` pair:

```text
1 + parameter_count × BASIS_ORDER.len()
```

`BASIS_ORDER.len()` is currently 15. A procedure with `P` parameters therefore performs `1 + 15P` complete dataflow solves per summary inference, allocating a fresh one-entry `HashMap` for every seeded scenario. Summary convergence may infer a procedure more than once.

`converge_summaries_with` then builds reverse dependencies from `InterproceduralAnalysis::direct_calls`, but the code documents that this graph misses callees in some nested substitutions. For soundness, every settled worklist is followed by a complete round-robin sweep of every procedure; any movement restarts convergence. This preserves correctness, but gives up the principal sparse-worklist benefit.

For `F` procedures, per-function dataflow cost `D`, average parameter count `P`, and `I` convergence rounds, the dominant term is approximately `O(I × F × (1 + 15P) × D)`, plus at least one `O(F)` completion inference sweep. The LSP’s salsa memoisation avoids recomputing unchanged procedures across many edits, but it does not remove the intrinsic cold cost, changed-procedure cost, incomplete dependency graph, or completion sweep.

## Corpus measurements

Release build, current `rust` tip `d834636aadd05658b2f8187af09c3a1425b9e7ed`, using `tcl-lsp-db/examples/tail_profile.rs`:

| file | lines | functions | `run_all_checks` | interprocedural taint | GVN + shimmer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `practcl.tcl` | 8,463 | 116 | ~196 ms | ~156 ms | ~21 ms |
| `parse_lemon.tcl` | 7,420 | 177 | ~55 ms | ~17 ms | ~32 ms |
| `filetypes.tcl` | 85,040 | 3 | ~37 ms | ~36 ms | <1 ms |

The `parse_lemon.tcl` control shows that taint is not universally dominant. On `practcl.tcl`, however, it is about 80% of `run_all_checks`; on the generated `filetypes.tcl`, it is nearly the entire checks phase even though other analysis costs dominate the overall edit.

Logs: `/tmp/tcl-lsp-audit-tail-profile.log`, `/tmp/tcl-lsp-audit-tail-profile-parse-lemon.log`, and `/tmp/tcl-lsp-audit-tail-profile-filetypes.log`.

## Algorithm/data-structure alternatives

1. **Multi-colour symbolic propagation (preferred investigation).** Assign bits to all `(parameter, taint-basis)` dependencies and propagate a compact bitset/dependency vector through the CFG once. Derive each return scenario from the final return dependency set. This changes the repeated-solve factor from `15P` full traversals to wider lattice operations in one traversal.
   - Dense bitsets are attractive for small/medium `P`.
   - A small inline bitset with spill storage avoids a heap allocation at most sites.
   - Sparse bitsets may win for very large parameter lists; benchmark both on the corpus.
2. **Transfer-function lattice.** Represent each SSA value as base taint plus a map from input parameter to basis transform. More expressive, but hashing/cloning maps at every join may cost more memory than bitsets.
3. **Batch one parameter at a time.** Carry all 15 bases in a fixed array and reduce from `15P` solves to `P`. Easier, but leaves a linear number of CFG traversals.
4. **Parallelise scenarios.** May reduce wall time but increases live memory/work and does not improve complexity; not a first choice.

Separately, make the call dependency graph complete from generic IR/registry-driven nested-script and command-prefix traversal, then converge by SCC condensation or reverse dirty worklist without an unconditional whole-module completion sweep. Do not add knowledge such as “if command is expr/eval/list” to the taint solver: evaluated bodies, command prefixes, callbacks, aliases, and indirection must come from `CommandRegistry` traits/roles/hooks and the shared IR.

Tcl concerns which must remain sound include `args`, namespace resolution, static/dynamic `rename`, `unknown`, `interp alias`, safe/sub-interpreters, traces/callbacks, `uplevel`/`upvar`, TclOO dispatch, shimmering, and recursively called SCCs.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

- Preserve byte-for-byte taint summaries and all diagnostics against the current solver on the #1181 corpus before switching.
- Add counters/benchmarks for propagation traversals, allocated bytes, summary reinferences, completion sweeps, and wall time.
- A procedure summary should no longer perform one whole CFG solve per `(parameter, basis)`.
- A complete dependency graph should allow removal of the unconditional completion sweep; retain a debug differential guard if useful.
- Keep incremental salsa reuse and prove a one-procedure edit re-executes only affected SCCs/callers.
- Document the chosen transfer representation, complexity, memory trade-offs, and conservative limits.

Test matrix:

- **TP:** direct and transitive taint, each basis, multiple parameters, `args`, aliases/upvars, callbacks/traces, TclOO methods, and safe/sub-interpreter boundaries.
- **FP:** sanitised/validated values, clean unused parameters, unreachable branches, and unrelated callers.
- **TN:** dynamic unresolved calls, `unknown`, overwritten commands after `rename`, and unsupported dialect commands conservatively abstain/widen as today.
- **FN:** nested command substitutions, list-built command prefixes, mutual recursion/SCCs, deep alias chains, namespace imports, and caller-frame indirection.
- Add compiler differential tests, native LSP diagnostic/latency e2e coverage, and a VS Code large-file diagnostics test with a generous but regression-sensitive bound.

Do not add clippy allows. If the solver API grows, replace the existing long positional argument list with named context structures rather than suppressing more lints.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: info-exists fold precision follow-ups: array-element guards never diagnosed; whole-class never-assigned instance vars could fold false
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
Two precision opportunities deliberately left on the safe side by the #1129 fix (which made the fold *abstain* on TclOO instance state — correct, since existence is a per-instance, call-order-dependent runtime fact; see the oracle transcripts on that issue).

## 1. Array-element guards are doubly conservative

The fold refuses any name containing non-alphanumerics, so `[info exists Params(key)]` never folded either way — before or after #1129. Sound, but the corpus idiom sits right next to the fixed one: SpiceGenTcl guards optional state with `if {[info exists Params]}` on names later array/dict-populated. An array *element* guard on a never-touched array is provably false in a plain proc; extending the fold to parse `name(elem)` and apply the same never-defined logic (with the same instance-state and scope-alias abstentions on the *array* name) would recover true positives at no soundness cost.

## 2. Whole-class never-assigned instance variables could fold false

Oracle case D (#1129): `oo::class create D { variable x; method m {} { info exists x } }` → `0` — a class-level `variable` declaration does **not** create the variable. If **no** method or constructor in the entire class ever assigns `x`, `[info exists x]` is provably `0` on every instance and could fold false instead of abstaining. The per-function fold cannot see this (it is a cross-method fact), but `MethodDef::instance_vars` is already the whole-class cross-block union (#1131), so a class-level pass could compute "declared but never assigned anywhere in the class" and thread it into `sccp::ExistenceFrame` as a third state (declared-and-assigned-somewhere → abstain; declared-never-assigned → fold false).

Caveats for 2: any `oo::objdefine`/dynamic definition evidence must widen back to abstention (see #1172 — objdefine bodies are currently invisible to lowering, so until that lands, presence of *any* objdefine on the class in workspace evidence should disable the refinement), and `unset`/`my variable`+set in mixins/superclasses along the MRO count as assignments.

Both found (and measured: the two corpus-wide post-fix survivors are genuine never-set locals, so today's precision is already good) during the #1129 fix.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Formatter hardcodes if/try/for grammar instead of registry roles
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

`tcl-lsp-core/src/formatting/engine.rs::identify_body_args` duplicates command grammar that the registry already knows:

- It special-cases the literal command name `for` so only argument 3 is formatted as a block, although the registry correctly marks arguments 0, 2, and 3 as semantic `ArgRole::Body`.
- It special-cases the literal command name `if` and scans every argument for `then`, `elseif`, or `else`.
- It special-cases the literal command name `try` and scans every argument for `on`, `trap`, or `finally`.
- The `if` and `try` registry role resolvers already return `ArgRole::Keyword` at the structurally valid positions, including malformed/incomplete-shape handling.

This is command-specific knowledge in a generic consumer and causes formatting drift for equivalent resolved commands.

## Reproduction

C Tcl treats an absolute global spelling as the same command. These are ordinary calls, not a dialect extension:

```tcl
::if {$x} then {
    puts yes
} else {
    puts no
}

::for {set i 0} {$i < 3} {incr i} {
    puts $i
}

::try {
    risky
} on error {msg opts} {
    puts $msg
}
```

The formatter’s direct `name == "if"`, `name == "for"`, and `name == "try"` branches do not apply to the leading-`::` forms. A provable static `rename` or `interp alias` has the same command grammar; a dynamic alias or `unknown` dispatch does not and must be left alone.

The current keyword loops also classify by word value rather than structural position. The registry resolvers are the C-Tcl-shaped parser and should decide whether an `else`/handler word is actually a keyword.

## Registry-first design

The semantic `ArgRole::Body` is not by itself enough for the `for` preference: start and next are Tcl scripts, but the formatter intentionally keeps them inline. Add formatting presentation data to the registry instead of erasing the semantic distinction or retaining a consumer branch. Possible shapes:

1. **Preferred:** a typed per-argument presentation descriptor (`InlineScript`, `BlockScript`, `Keyword`, `ParameterList`, etc.) resolved alongside `ArgRole`.
2. A narrower `block_body_roles`/callback returning the body arguments which should expand. Less data, but risks another parallel role system.
3. A formatter hook ID. Use only if the layout cannot be expressed as data; a hook still belongs to the registry and must dispatch generically.
4. Stripping leading `::` in the formatter. Reject as a partial patch: it leaves grammar duplicated and does not cover static aliases/renames or new dialect commands.

The formatter should consume the existing `ArgRole::Keyword` results for `if`/`try`, and the new presentation descriptor for the `for` distinction.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

- No command-name checks for `if`, `try`, or `for` remain in the formatting engine.
- Bare, leading-`::`, namespace-resolved, and provable static alias/rename forms format identically.
- Same-named user procedures and dynamic command heads are not reformatted as built-ins.
- Formatting remains idempotent and semantics-preserving for incomplete/malformed input.
- The registry documentation explains semantic body roles versus formatter presentation roles, with plain-English examples and limits.

Test matrix:

- **TP:** all valid `if` clause shapes, repeated `elseif`, implicit/explicit `then`, every `try` handler shape, and `for` start/test/next/body.
- **FP:** a user proc named `if` in a namespace, data words equal to `else`/`on`, an overwritten command after `rename`, and a hidden command in a safe interpreter.
- **TN:** dynamic head, dynamic alias, malformed clause, unsupported dialect/version, and `unknown` fallback.
- **FN:** leading-`::`, static `rename`, static `interp alias`, nesting in `namespace eval`/`uplevel`, and TclOO method bodies.
- Add `tcl-lsp-core` formatter unit tests, native LSP whole/range-formatting e2e tests, and VS Code format-document/format-selection tests.

Do not add clippy allows; prefer a named registry descriptor/context type.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Tk widget/geometry analyser state is not keyed by interpreter domain — false TK1001 and missed TK1002 across `interp create` / `child eval` isolation
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
The Tk-specific diagnostics TK1001 (geometry-manager conflict) and TK1002 (widget references a non-existent parent) are computed from a single flat, un-namespaced pair of analyser fields shared across the whole file walk, while every other kind of analyser state — procs, variables, safe-interp hidden/exposed sets — is already saved and restored around a child interpreter's eval body by the shared isolation helper. A child interpreter that has loaded Tk has a completely separate window hierarchy, so a widget path used in both the child's body and the parent script is two unrelated windows; conflating them produces a false positive in one direction and a false negative in the other. This is a single-finding issue because the mechanism is Tk-state-specific, but the fix is the campaign's established isolation pattern applied to one more piece of state.

### idx 91 — tk (`safe_interp`)

`dialog1.tcl`'s own pattern (`interp create child; load {} Tk child; child eval { …creates '.', '.t'… }`) gives the child a separate Tk hierarchy; a same-named widget path used inside the child body and in the parent script is conflated, producing both a false TK1001 and a false-negative TK1002.

Repro pointer: audit `91/` — `dialog1_repro_tk1001.tcl` (`interp create child; load {} Tk child; child eval { frame .top; pack .top.a }; frame .top; grid .top.b` → false TK1001), `dialog1_repro_tk1002.tcl`, `control_tk1001_conflict.tcl` and `control_tk1002_missing_parent.tcl` (the true-positive controls), and `oracle_interp_isolation.tcl` (proves the isolation generally: a command defined inside `child eval {…}` never appears in the parent's `info commands`, the mechanism Tk widget-creation commands rely on to register their path as a command).

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints may be stale against current code):

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs:214` and `:218` (`tk_created_widgets: HashSet<String>`, `tk_geometry: BTreeMap<String, TkGeometryUsage>` — single flat fields on `Analyser`, never keyed by interpreter domain) read/written from `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/tk_checks.rs:147-194` (`emit_tk_checks`) and flushed in `tk_checks.rs:282-314` (`flush_tk_geometry_diagnostics`). The isolation boundary that should scope them already exists for every other kind of analyser state (procs, vars, safe-interp hidden/exposed sets) in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:1176-1240` (`isolate_interp_eval_body`, called from both the literal `interp eval PATH {…}` handler at handlers.rs:1106 and the `NAME eval {…}` handle-form handler at handlers.rs:1278 `handle_interp_handle_eval_command` — exactly the `child eval {…}` spelling used in dialog1.tcl) — it pushes/pops `self.interp_path_stack` and `self.safe_interp_stack` around the child body walk but has no equivalent push/pop (or domain-keying) for `tk_created_widgets`/`tk_geometry`, so `emit_tk_checks` (dispatched per-command from commands.rs:960 inside `emit_dispatch_site_diagnostics`, which runs unconditionally for every command including ones inside an isolated child body) sees and pollutes the same global sets regardless of which interpreter's widget hierarchy a given `frame`/`pack`/`grid` call actually belongs to.

### Fix direction

Two campaign mechanisms cover this without new invention. `isolate_interp_eval_body` (STATUS.md §4: "if a third spelling of *run this script in an isolated child-interpreter scope* turns up, extend this, not a new parallel implementation") is the one place both `interp eval PATH {…}` and handle-form `NAME eval {…}` pass through, so the save/restore belongs there alongside the existing `interp_path_stack`/`safe_interp_stack` handling. If per-domain accumulation is wanted rather than plain save/restore — TK1002 wants "does this parent exist *in this hierarchy*", which is per-domain rather than per-block — the `@interp@<path>` synthetic-key pattern (§4) is the established way to give an unrepresentable domain a stable identity, keying `tk_created_widgets`/`tk_geometry` by interpreter path so two identical widget paths in two domains are never the same widget. The flush in `flush_tk_geometry_diagnostics` needs to follow whichever shape is chosen. Worth pinning both directions (FP: the isolated pair no longer conflicts; TN: the genuine same-domain conflict still fires — the existing `control_*` repros are ready-made) plus a TK1002 case for the false-negative half.

Split from #1019; the audit JSON entry is authoritative for repro detail.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: E001 misses a bare TclOO object command produced by command substitution
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

The analyser has an explicitly documented false negative for a TclOO object command used directly from `[…]`.

```tcl
oo::class create Dog {
    method bark {} {return woof}
}
[Dog new]
```

C Tcl 9.0.3 executes `Dog new`, obtains an object command, then invokes that object with no method. It errors:

```text
wrong # args: should be "::oo::Obj… method ?arg ...?"
-errorcode {TCL WRONGARGS}
```

Current `tcl diag --dialect tcl9.0 --json` reports no diagnostics.

The test `fn_e001_bare_command_substitution_head_not_covered` asserts this absence as an accepted gap. The `$object` bare-dispatch path can emit E001, but the command-substitution-head path only validates a named method and has no equivalent arity machinery.

## Fix direction

Represent command-producing expressions and object-handle types in the shared interprocedural value/type lattice. A generic invocation consumer should receive:

- possible command identities/object classes;
- whether a TclOO invocation has a method word;
- static/dynamic target confidence;
- interpreter/namespace domain.

Do not add a `[Dog new]` or TclOO constructor spelling check to the diagnostic walker. Constructors, aliases, factories, renamed commands, and registry-declared object-returning commands should flow through data.

Dynamic/ambiguous command results should abstain or emit the existing lower-confidence diagnostic, not E001.

## Tests and acceptance

- E001 fires on a provably TclOO object invoked without a method through direct `[Class new]`, a variable, proc return, alias, and constructor/factory flow.
- Correct method calls, non-object command substitutions, dynamic/unknown results, same-named user commands, safe/sub-interpreters, and unsupported dialects stay silent.
- Include TP/FP/TN/FN analyser tests, remove/flip the accepted-gap assertion, native diagnostic e2e, and VS Code diagnostic/range tests.
- Validate against C Tcl 9 completion codes and test older Tcl/dialect availability.
- Document the confidence boundary and examples.

Do not add clippy allows; command/object behaviour must remain registry/lattice driven.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: BPF-Tcl: build typed event schemas, handler composition, and loader/link lifecycle
TkActive substring guard forces full analysis on non-Tk corpus files
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

The per-item analyser’s `TkActive` gate is a whole-source substring conjunction:

```rust
dialect == "tk"
    || (source.contains("package")
        && source.contains("require")
        && source.contains("Tk"))
```

The three words may occur anywhere, in unrelated commands, data, regexes, generated prose, or comments. A match forces `analyse_per_item_with` to abandon all per-body memoisation and run a complete whole-file analysis on every edit.

This is both a false-positive classification bug and a large-project performance cliff. Command/package activation knowledge must come from structured parsing and the registry, not substring coincidence.

## Current corpus evidence

Release build at `d834636aadd05658b2f8187af09c3a1425b9e7ed`:

```text
cargo run --release -p tcl-compiler --example per_item_fallbacks
corpus: 1103 files, 567638 lines

FAST PATH             908 files, 305882 lines, 9346 ms
fell back             195 files, 261756 lines, 7712 ms
tk-active              49 files, 148823 lines, 3618 ms
```

`TkActive` alone accounts for 26.2% of all corpus lines and 21.2% of the sweep’s total analysis time.

The two slowest false-positive examples:

- `tcllib/modules/fumagic/filetypes.tcl` (85,040 lines): `tk-active`, ~1,851 ms analyser time. It has `package require Tcl` near the top and unrelated literal `Tcl/Tk script text executable` deep in generated magic data. It does not `package require Tk`.
- `tcllib/modules/practcl/practcl.tcl` (8,463 lines): `tk-active`, ~202 ms analyser time. It has many package operations and tests `[package provide Tk]`, but does not require Tk.

The production-tail profiler measured:

| file | `file_analysis_incremental` per edit | compiler checks per edit | both production queries |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `filetypes.tcl` | ~1,831 ms | ~1,365 ms | ~2,742 ms |
| `practcl.tcl` | ~229 ms | ~238 ms | ~377 ms |

Diagnostics run asynchronously, so this does not block the LSP message loop, but it burns CPU after every settled edit and delays fresh diagnostics.

The existing design doc already records a prior audit in which about 78% of `TkActive` hits were false positives. This ticket makes that known design finding actionable and pins current measurements.

## Registry-first fix direction

Resolve actual package activation from structured command facts:

1. Recognise a statically resolvable `package require Tk` invocation through the `package` command spec/subcommand data, including leading-`::`, namespace resolution, and option/version words.
2. Treat the explicit `tk` dialect as active without scanning.
3. For dynamic package names or commands reached via `rename`, `unknown`, aliases, `eval`, safe/sub-interpreters, or traces, use existing analyser facts where provable; otherwise choose a documented conservative policy.
4. Long term, represent Tk geometry state as a small mergeable per-item fact so a genuinely Tk file can keep per-item analysis. Tightening activation is the immediate safe win; incrementalising Tk checks is a separate second step.

Alternatives:

- **Signature/command scan using registry roles (preferred immediate fix):** linear once, exact, and reuses existing Tcl parsing.
- **Search for the exact bytes `package require Tk`:** faster but still wrong for whitespace, continuations, `::package`, comments/quotes, abbreviations, and aliases.
- **Regex:** same semantic problem as exact bytes.
- **Always run Tk checks:** avoids false negatives but permanently destroys the fast path.
- **Disable Tk checks outside `tk` dialect:** fast but misses ordinary `.tcl` files which legitimately execute `package require Tk`.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Inline-proc refactor ignores defaults, `args`, and Tcl substitution context
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Problem

`inline_proc_action` maps written call words to parameters and textually replaces `$param` references with the raw source spelling. It does not implement Tcl procedure binding or value substitution.

### Default argument

```tcl
proc f {{name world}} {
    puts "hello $name"
}
f
```

C Tcl 9.0.3 prints `hello world`. The inline action has no written argument to substitute and emits `puts "hello $name"` in the caller, which errors because `name` is unset.

### Context-sensitive substitution

```tcl
proc f {name} {
    puts "hello $name"
}
f {a b}
```

Original output is `hello a b`. Raw splicing emits `puts "hello {a b}"`, which prints `hello {a b}`. Source syntax for an argument is not the same as its runtime value when inserted inside a quoted word, array index, expression, or command substitution.

The action also does not bind `args`, reject excess/missing arguments, preserve local variables/frame identity, or account for aliases, traces, namespace context, TclOO, `return`, and registry-declared frame-sensitive commands comprehensively.

## Fix direction

Do not textually substitute raw call words. Inline through a Tcl-aware IR transform:

- perform full proc argument binding, including defaults and `args`;
- preserve evaluation count/order and caller substitution semantics, normally by introducing hygienic temporaries;
- alpha-rename locals against caller variables and aliases;
- preserve completion-code/frame behaviour or decline;
- require a resolved, non-renamed/non-aliased target with complete call-site evidence;
- use registry effects/roles/hooks for frame-sensitive and evaluated-code behaviour.

A conservative immediate fix is to offer inlining only for zero-parameter, single-command, frame-independent procs with no locals or control transfer.

## Tests and acceptance

- Differentially execute original/inlined programs under C Tcl 9, comparing output, result/options, traces, and variable state.
- TP/FP/TN/FN: required/default/`args` formals, braced/quoted/expanded args, side-effecting arguments, repeated/unused params, local collisions, arrays, namespaces, aliases/rename, TclOO, safe/sub-interpreters, and errors.
- Add core IR/refactor tests, native LSP grouped-edit e2e, and VS Code apply tests.
- Document the supported subset and refusal reasons with examples.

Do not add clippy allows.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Variable propagation in method bodies needs an instance-variable escaping model (propagation.rs vs elimination.rs asymmetry)
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
Found during the `[self class]` folding PR (#1095). The general SCCP propagation pass deliberately stays OFF for method bodies: an instance variable is object state that outlives the frame, and any `my …` call can rewrite it, so `set ivar 1; my other; puts $ivar` would be miscompiled by the per-function constants lattice. `elimination.rs` already has the escaping model for this; `propagation.rs` does not — #1095 worked around it with a dedicated no-constants-map walk (`run_oo_method_folds`) that folds only `[self class]`.

Consequence: `$var` propagation, `[string …]` folds over method-local variables, and the `${ns}` hop of the ticklecharts chain (`set ns [namespace qualifiers [self class]]; ${ns}::setdef`) don't fold inside methods even when provably safe (a method-local `set` never aliased by instance state).

Fix direction: port/share elimination.rs's escaping classification into the propagation lattice — a variable is propagatable inside a method body iff it's provably method-local (never declared via `variable`, not in the class's variable list, not touched through `my variable`/`upvar`), with `my`/`next`/`[self …]` dispatches acting as barriers only for escaping variables. Abstain-toward-no-fold stays the rule. Blocks the second half of #1096's chain; also unblocks the deliberate narrowing documented in #1095.

uncatalogued_candidates.title: Interprocedural call-site seeding wrongly seeds a module's own `unknown` handler
uncatalogued_candidates.body:
## Summary

A module that defines its own `proc unknown {cmd args}` gets that procedure's parameters seeded as compile-time constants from its *direct* callers alone — but Tcl also dispatches **every unresolved command word in the module** to it. Those dispatches are invisible to the scan, so a coincidentally-uniform set of direct calls folds a condition that varies at runtime. Same false-positive shape as #969, in the one procedure whose callers the scan structurally cannot enumerate.

This is the last residual gap left open by #1043 (which closed #976 and #978).

## Reproduction

```tcl
proc unknown {cmd args} {
    if {$cmd eq "alpha"} { return 1 } else { return 2 }
}
unknown alpha
unknown alpha
bogus beta
```

`bogus` names no command, so Tcl invokes `unknown bogus beta` — `cmd` is `"bogus"`, and the `else` branch is live.

Measured against `collect_call_site_constants` on `rust` at `2680ae7`, and unchanged by #1043:

```
slot0 (::unknown, param `cmd`) = (["alpha"], false)
enumerates_every_caller()      = true
```

The scan asserts it saw every caller and binds `cmd` to the constant `"alpha"`, so `$cmd eq "alpha"` folds to true and I230 fires on a condition that is genuinely runtime-varying.

**Oracle caveat, stated plainly:** the container I confirmed this in has no `tclsh`, so unlike the other follow-ups from this campaign there is no attached oracle transcript. The compiler-side measurement above is real; the Tcl-side claim rests on documented `unknown` semantics (`Tcl_SetVar`-era behaviour unchanged through 9.0 — an unresolved command name is dispatched to `unknown` with the name and its arguments prepended). Worth a 30-second `tclsh` confirmation by whoever picks this up before writing the fix, per the bar #979 sets.

## Why it wasn't fixed in #1043

The fix needs the scan to treat *every* command word that resolves to no known procedure as a call site for `::unknown` — but only when the module actually defines one, and only under a dialect where `unknown` is the handler. That last part is the blocker: it wants a registry fact marking the handler (so no consumer spells the name `unknown`, matching the rule that nothing per-command is hardcoded in `call_site_scan.rs`), and `Traits` is **currently full at 64 bits**. So this is a bitfield widening plus a new trait, not a one-line flag — deliberately left rather than rushed at the end of an already-large change.

Note that `namespace unknown` and `package unknown` are already covered and are *not* this bug: the registry declares their handler argument `ArgRole::CommandPrefix`, and #1043 records command-prefix callbacks as real call sites.

## Suggested shape

1. Widen `Traits` past 64 bits (or find a cheaper carrier for handler-ness), and mark the dialect's unresolved-command handler.
2. In `call_site_scan`, when `resolve_target` returns `None` for a literal command word and the module defines the handler, record an invocation of it with the word plus its arguments — the same `record_invocation` path everything else uses.
3. Conservative fallback if step 1 is judged not worth it: if the module defines the handler at all, flag `opaque_callee` and withdraw every seed in the module. Sound, cheap, and blunt — a module with an `unknown` handler loses all interprocedural folding.

## Verification bar

The repro above as a failing-then-passing test in `call_site_scan.rs`, plus TP/FP/TN/FN around it: a module with **no** `unknown` handler must be unaffected (this is the regression risk — it is the common case); a handler with direct callers that genuinely agree *and* no unresolved words in the module should still seed. Full `cargo test -p tcl-compiler --lib`, `make check-all`, no new clippy allows.

## References

- Root issue: #969 · fix PR: #970
- Sibling follow-ups: #976, #977, #978, #979, #980
- PR that closed #976/#978 and documented this gap: #1043
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/call_site_scan.rs` (`resolve_target`, `record_invocation`, `CallSiteEvidence::opaque_callee`); audit trail in `docs/design/compiler/fp-audit-todo.md` (`FP-IPCP-02`)
